scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5121: HELP!! My computer (PC1 in Office A) and my
neighbour's (PC2, literally the next desk) have STOPPED SPEAKING to each
other -- yesterday I was pulling files off it fine, today nothing on it
answers me at all. The switch our desks plug into has obviously died (or
PC2's port on it has) -- there is nothing else between two desks!! Please
restart the office switch, or turn PC2's port back on, and make our computers
talk again -- we have a handover due!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC1 and PC2 are both in Office A VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other
  directly over the access switch with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the intra-office L2
  path -- does the agent verify PC1<->PC2 reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate an access-switch/port fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC1 cannot reach
its neighbor PC2 on the same VLAN -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100)
reaches PC2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% loss. Both hosts sit in Office A VLAN10 on
the 10.1.0.0/24 subnet and are bridged by the access switch; the traffic stays
local (same subnet, no routing or gateway involved) and the L2 forwarding path
between the two ports is intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-office path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC1->PC2 on the live lab, confirms both hosts are up on 10.1.0.0/24 and that
ARP/L2 forwarding works on the access switch, finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a downed access-switch
port, a VLAN10 misconfiguration, or DSWA1 to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough five-layer investigation found no network fault consistent with the reported symptom. The complaint that PC1 and PC2 have "stopped speaking to each other" was tested directly: bidirectional ICMP between pc1 (10.1.0.100) and pc2 (10.1.0.101) returned 0% packet loss in both directions, with sub-millisecond round-trip times, confirming the path is fully operational right now.

The infra_sweep flagged a drop rule on dswa1 and dswa2 (`iifname "br0.10" ip saddr 10.1.0.0/24 ip daddr 10.3.0.0/24`), but a direct query (`nft list ruleset`) on those devices returned an empty ruleset — the rule exists in a configuration file on disk but has never been loaded into the live kernel. No traffic is being blocked, which is confirmed by successful pings from pc1 and pc2 to pc3 (10.3.0.100) as well. The l2_snapshot found zero duplicate MAC addresses. The OSPF fabric is fully converged: csw1 holds six Full adjacencies including dswb2, and every core/distribution device carries 32 OSPF routes. The tc_snapshot showed only baseline fq_codel qdiscs with zero shaping. The pressure_sweep found no stress processes, CPU load, or socket pressure on any device.

The user's assumption that PC1 and PC2 share a single access switch is also incorrect: PC1 attaches through aswa2, while PC2 attaches through aswa3 — separate switches with dual redundant uplinks to dswa1 and dswa2. No flap script, carrier counter spike, DHCP failure, or syslog evidence of a past outage was found. The claim is unconfirmed and is most likely a transient perception error or a test of a higher-layer service (e.g., file-share application) rather than a network-layer failure.

Root cause: No network-layer fault exists; the reported symptom is unconfirmed by any live evidence.
Fix: No corrective action is required at the network layer. Advise the user to retest and verify any application-layer service they rely on independently of basic ICMP.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 and PC2 are both up on VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other directly over the access switch at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent confirmed both hosts (10.1.0.100 and 10.1.0.101) are reachable with 0% loss and referenced the VLAN interface (br0.10) and L2 checks, demonstrating they are up on 10.1.0.0/24 and the L2 path is healthy.

The agent's logs contain direct, relevant measurements (bidirectional pings between PC1/PC2, pings to PC3, nft output, OSPF neighbor and link state checks) that support the conclusion that no network-layer fault is present; a few minor assertions (exact access-switch ports) are not explicitly shown in the log. Overall the investigation justifiably rules out the reported intra-VLAN outage.
